text:
alex.w: Quick sync to lock down Juno Health POC scope — want to align use cases, success criteria, security blockers, and a rough 6-week timeline. Can we agree on top 3 endpoints and what 'success' looks like?

june.j (Juno Health): Top priority is clinical summarization (ED + discharge notes), de-identification of PHI, and a clinician-facing Q&A assistant. Latency target: 95th < 300ms for short notes. Success = 90% clinician accept rate in blind eval + no PHI leakage in redaction tests.

maria.s: Noted. For POC endpoints I'd propose: 1) /clinical-summary (structured bullets), 2) /deid-redact (redaction + masked output), 3) /clinician-assist (follow-up Qs). We'll need a ~200-sample prompt/eval set for each. Can you share sample notes (synthetic or redacted) and top 10 clinician prompts?

june.j (Juno Health): We can provide 500 de-identified notes and a small gold set. Will need a non-prod VPC option if we test with real data.

secops-liaison-bot: Security checklist: SOC2 report, encryption at rest (customer KMS), TLS 1.2+, IP allowlist / VPC peering, Data Processing Agreement + DPA addendum for PHI. We require completed security questionnaire (we can send), and network review ~10 business days once we have network diagram.

sam.ae: For pricing: hosted API estimate vs dedicated: if you run 2M tokens/month for summaries and 1M tokens for assist, hosted would be usage-based ~ $X/month (ballpark). Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput (SLA) starts with a monthly commit — we can run a sizing call after finalizing token profile. Also note extra for Private (on-prem/VPC) + support. I'll draft a simple cost comparison.

maria.s: Operational success criteria I'd track: throughput (requests/sec), 95th token latency, token cost per summary, and quality metrics: ROUGE-L / entity-preservation and hallucination rate <5%. We'll run blind clinician evals (N=50 per endpoint) and automatic checks for PHI leakage using regex + entity models.

alex.w: Timeline proposal: Week 0: legal + sec questionnaire complete; Week 1: data handoff (redacted samples), Week 2: model/quant config + initial endpoints, Week 3: internal eval + quick fixes, Week 4: clinician blind evals, Week 5: resilience and SLO tuning, Week 6: wrap + decision. Anyone see blockers?

june.j (Juno Health): Security review is the biggest risk. Also SSO (SAML) for clinician sandbox. Can we do IP allowlist + private link for the POC?

maria.s: Yes — we can do VPC peering or Private Link for Dedicated; SSO support available for staging. For IP allowlist we need the subnet list from you.

secops-liaison-bot: We'll also need an inventory of third-party models/weights used and quantization details for the audit. Provide the model mapping doc before Week 1 handoff.

sam.ae: Action items: 1) I'll send a short cost comparison by EOD, 2) Maria will share eval prompt templates and a curl example, 3) June to send data sample + network contact, 4) Sec ops to send questionnaire.

maria.s: Curl example for quick smoke (replace KEY/URL):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-clinical-v1","input":"Summarize: {{note_text}}","max_tokens":256}'
```

maria.s: Also attaching suggested eval rubric: precision/recall on entities, clinician accept % (binary), hallucination flag rate.

alex.w: Great — let's schedule 30m sync on Monday to finalize the questionnaire assignee and confirm the VPC flow. I'll invite June + secops + Maria.

june.j (Juno Health): Monday works. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
